dct_description_sm: The Beaufort Delta and the high Arctic communities of the Northwest Territories (NWT) are experiencing the most rapid climate warming in Canada. Communities are experiencing greater changes in the active layer of the permafrost relative to other regions in the NWT. The current and past hazardous waste management practices pose a risk to the integrity of the ecosystem because hazardous waste are contaminants that when released, can have long lasting negative effects on drinking water as well as aquatic and animal life. The thawing permafrost increases the pathways for contaminants to spread to the greater environment and heightens the need to have effective hazardous waste management to prevent the release of contaminants. This project aimed to mitigate the climate change risk posed by hazardous waste that are currently stockpiled in community governments by arranging for qualified professionals to visit and inventory the nature and quantity of hazardous waste located in several community government facilities.  The project then involved the application of a climate change risk management protocol to assess the relative risk of the hazardous waste in eight communities.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Adaptation
dct_title_s: Hazardous Waste Risk Assessment Pilot Project Beaufort Delta/High Arctic Communities
